headline: BHP PORT HEDLAND WORKERS VOTE 100% YES TO STRIKE — Pilbara Iron Ore Exports at Risk from World's Largest Loading Hub
snippet: BHP's electrical workers at Port Hedland, Western Australia voted 100% in favour of strike action on June 11 — following six months of stalled wage negotiations covering approximately 450 port workers. The Electrical Trades Union has authorized work stoppages ranging from 30 minutes to 24 hours. Port Hedland is the world's largest iron ore loading hub and the exclusive export gateway for BHP's entire Pilbara iron ore production; any disruption raises the risk of tightening seaborne supply at a moment when Chinese steel mills are already navigating elevated input costs, with downstream knock-on effects for mining construction timelines globally.

headline: GOLD MINERS BULLISH PERCENT INDEX HITS ZERO: "TOTAL CAPITULATION" — Contrarians Flag Most Extreme Oversold Reading Since 2016
snippet: The Gold Miners Bullish Percent Index — which measures the percentage of gold mining stocks on Point and Figure buy signals — crashed from 100 in January 2026 to zero in June, its most extreme reading since the 2016 and 2020 cycle lows. Contrarian analysts are flagging the reading as a rare "total capitulation" signal: a zero BPI means every single component stock in the sector has simultaneously flipped to a sell signal, a condition that has historically preceded the most violent and sustained recoveries in gold equities rather than additional downside. For self-directed junior mining investors, the setup mirrors the 2016 bottom, when BPI zeroed before gold stocks delivered their best 12-month return in a decade.

headline: ROCKY SHORE GOLD DISCOVERS BULK-STYLE ZONE ON NEWFOUNDLAND'S APPLETON FAULT — 400m × 600m Open, Program Triples to 12,500m
snippet: Rocky Shore Gold Ltd. (CSE: RSG) reported June 10 the discovery of a near-surface bulk-style gold zone at the Lane Pond Gold Target within its 100%-owned Gold Anchor Project in central Newfoundland — intersected in eight widely-spaced holes over 400 metres of strike and 600 metres down-dip from 50 to 240 metres vertical depth, interpreted as associated with the prolific Appleton Fault. The company immediately tripled its planned drill program from 3,500 to 12,500 metres in response to the scale of the zone, with assay results pending for the majority of holes. Gold Anchor already hosts an existing mineral resource estimate, and the Lane Pond bulk-tonnage concept represents conceptually district-scale potential within Canada's most active emerging gold belt.

headline: ERO COPPER CONFIRMS FURNAS HIGH-GRADE BELT: 52,000m ASSAYED, 10 RIGS, EARN-IN 2 YEARS AHEAD OF SCHEDULE — Central Zone Opens
snippet: Ero Copper Corp. (TSX/NASDAQ: ERO) released June 10 assay results for an additional 24,000 metres of drilling at the Furnas Copper-Gold Project in Brazil's Carajás Mineral Province, bringing total reported results to approximately 52,000 of 75,000+ metres drilled through May 2026. Results confirmed high-grade continuity in the northwest and southeast zones with a new central zone identified as a third structural corridor. Ten drill rigs are currently operating on site, and Ero is on track to complete all three earn-in drilling programs roughly two years ahead of schedule — accelerating its path to a 60% ownership stake in one of the most aggressively drilled copper-gold systems in the Americas during the current deficit cycle.

headline: CRITICAL ELEMENTS ROSE WEST LITHIUM FOOTPRINT GROWS 6X IN SIX MONTHS — 10,000m SUMMER PROGRAM UNDERWAY ON 1,250m × 800m SYSTEM
source_name: Investing News Network / Critical Elements Lithium
snippet: Critical Elements Lithium Corporation (TSXV: CRE) announced June 9 the launch of a 10,000-metre systematic summer 2026 drill program at the Rose West Discovery in Quebec's James Bay region — following a Winter 2026 program that expanded the mineralized footprint approximately six-fold, from 450m × 370m in early 2024 to a current 1,250m × 800m system hosting multiple lithium-tantalum-bearing pegmatites in both hanging wall and footwall positions. Two drill rigs are now operating on a 100-metre grid. The six-fold footprint expansion in six months makes Rose West one of the fastest-growing lithium discoveries in the James Bay district, which continues to attract intense attention from battery-material developers and EV supply chain strategists.

headline: BRUNSWICK EXPLORATION: ANAIS LITHIUM EXTENDS TO 350m WIDE × 600m LONG — 1.13% Li2O Over 27.4m in Latest Step-Out
snippet: Brunswick Exploration Inc. (TSXV: BRW) released June 10 final assay results from its 2026 winter drilling campaign at the Anatacau Main Project in Quebec — confirming the Anais Main pegmatite system has grown to over 350 metres wide and 600 metres long, with the latest step-out hole (AN-26-12) returning 1.13% Li2O over 27.4 metres at shallow depths and the system remaining open in all directions. Eastern extension holes also returned elevated cesium and tantalum values, confirming the pegmatite system remains fractionated outside the main structural corridor and expanding the prospective ground around the main dyke. Brunswick's next campaign is planned for late Q3-2026.

headline: PBOC BUYS GOLD FOR SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE MONTH — 60,000 oz Added in May, China's Total Hits 73.83M oz and 7% of Reserves
snippet: The People's Bank of China added 60,000 troy ounces to its official gold reserves in May 2026 — the seventh consecutive month of net additions — bringing total Chinese official gold holdings to 73.83 million ounces, equivalent to approximately 7% of China's international reserve assets, up from roughly 3.5% at the start of the current accumulation cycle. For gold investors watching supply-demand fundamentals, Chinese central bank demand represents a structural, price-insensitive buyer base that maintains its accumulation regardless of spot price — a persistent demand floor that reinforces the thesis of institutional year-end targets clustering $5,500–$6,300/oz even as Western paper selling drives the current June correction.

headline: GOLDSEEK: SPIKING INFLATION COULD SEND REAL YIELDS LOWER — The Counterintuitive Macro Case for Gold Heading into FOMC June 17
snippet: A June 9 analysis circulated by GoldSeek argues that the same Iran-conflict inflation shock suppressing gold could paradoxically turn bullish if nominal CPI rises faster than the Fed can anchor expectations — a scenario where real yields (nominal rate minus inflation) actually decline despite nominal rate hikes, which is the precise condition under which gold historically performs best. The analytical framework: real yields drive gold more reliably than nominal rates, and an oil shock large enough to push CPI above 5–6% could overwhelm any 25–50 basis-point Fed move, sending inflation-adjusted Treasury returns negative. With Kevin Warsh's first FOMC press conference on June 17 set to define policy trajectory for the remainder of 2026, this framework is the essential context for investors positioning into the decision.

headline: P2 GOLD'S GABBS NEVADA ON TRACK FOR Q4 FEASIBILITY — Water Rights Secured, Second Rig Mobilizing August for Walker Lane Gold-Copper
snippet: P2 Gold Inc. (TSXV: PGLD) provided a June 9 update confirming the Gabbs gold-copper project in Nevada's Walker Lane Trend remains on track for a Q4 2026 feasibility study — with RC infill drilling of the Lucky Strike Zone ongoing and expanded due to positive results, a second drill rig mobilizing in early August for the Sullivan higher-grade resources down-dip, and a definitive agreement signed for the acquisition of 2,500 acre-feet per year of water rights with Nevada state approval anticipated to coincide with the FS completion. Walker Lane continues to attract senior producer attention as a low-jurisdiction-risk copper-gold belt, and a completed feasibility study would position Gabbs as a fully financed M&A target or construction-decision candidate at a time when development-stage gold-copper assets command record acquirer premiums.

headline: MP MATERIALS OR USA RARE EARTH: WHICH WINS THE JUNE BATTLE? — Analysts Size Up $11.6B vs $6B Race to Build America's Rare Earth Supply Chain
snippet: A June 8 Motley Fool analysis pits the two dominant U.S. rare earth companies against each other as investors navigate China's MOFCOM export licensing delays and dysprosium prices up 105% year-to-date: MP Materials (NYSE: MP, $11.6B), which posted record Q1 NdPr production of 917 metric tons (+63% YoY) and has "imminent" heavy REE separation commissioning at Mountain Pass with Apple and GM supply contracts, versus USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR, $6B), which commissioned Phase 1a of its Stillwater magnet manufacturing plant with $6M in Q1 revenue and a $1.6B CHIPS Act DOC award funding its mine-to-magnet ambitions. Both companies represent investable proxies for the Western REE supply chain buildout — the key differentiator being that MP operates a producing mine today while USAR's Round Top deposit is still in development.
